symbols.k: the number of classes a node's examples can belong to
symbols.A: an attribute (feature) that a tree node can test or split on
symbols.x: the value of an input feature
symbols.X: an input feature (attribute) of an example, such as length
symbols.S: the set of training examples at the node being split
symbols.sum: add up the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.Y: the target (output) values of a set of examples
symbols.p: the share (proportion) of examples in the set that belong to one class
symbols.h: the bandwidth: how far from the query point a training point still counts
symbols.i: counts the subsets or branches a split creates
symbols.log: logarithm, here base 2 (so entropy is measured in bits)
symbols.abs: size of a set (number of examples in it), or absolute value of a number
symbols.m: the number of examples in a subset
symbols.n: the number of training examples (or values) in the data
symbols.j: counts the classes, one term per class
symbols.B: a second attribute or true/false variable
symbols.H: entropy of a set: how mixed its classes are
symbols.w:gain: information gain: how much a split reduces entropy
symbols.nu: one possible value of attribute A
symbols.y: the target value of an example
symbols.w:entropy: how mixed the classes in a set are: 0 if pure, larger if mixed
symbols.bar:y: the mean of the target values in a subset
symbols.u: the input to the kernel: distance to the query point divided by bandwidth
symbols.C: a third attribute or true/false variable
symbols.E: the entropy of a set, as a number
symbols.in: is an element of, ranges over the values in
symbols.N: a No example (count of negatives), as in [3Y,2N]
symbols.f: false, as in a test outcome X = f; the true function in smoothing
symbols.w:mse: mean squared error of a subset: average squared gap from the subset's mean
symbols.hat:f: the smoother's estimate of the true function at a point
symbols.K: the kernel: turns a scaled distance into a weight
symbols.d: the depth of the tree (number of levels of splits)
symbols.t: true, as in a test outcome X = t
symbols.R: the expected loss of an action; elsewhere a rectangular region of inputs
symbols.c: a single constant value a leaf predicts
symbols.w: the weight a training point gets in a prediction
symbols.hat:y: the model's predicted value for the target
symbols.T: the set of target values (examples) reaching a node
symbols.D: a fourth attribute or true/false variable
symbols.w:values: the set of possible values of an attribute
symbols.w:splitentropy: entropy of the branch sizes alone: how finely the attribute chops the data, ignoring labels
symbols.w:cost: what it costs to measure an attribute
symbols.alpha: a possible action or prediction we could choose
symbols.mid: given: the probability or loss is conditioned on what follows
symbols.lambda: the loss: how costly an action is if a given class is the truth
symbols.pi: the constant 3.14159, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter
symbols.w:sd: standard deviation: typical spread of the values around their mean
symbols.norm: the distance (length) between two points; subscript 2 means ordinary straight-line distance
symbols.epsilon: random noise added to the true function value
symbols.w:gini: Gini impurity: another score for how mixed a node is, 0 if pure
symbols.w:gainratio: information gain divided by split entropy
symbols.w:sdr: standard deviation reduction: spread before the split minus weighted spread after
symbols.w:playtennis: the label we predict: whether tennis is played that day
symbols.w:predicted class: the class the tree predicts for the example
symbols.w:class: a class (category) the example might truly belong to
symbols.v: one possible value of an attribute
symbols.l: the number of subsets a split creates
symbols.w:weighted average variance: variance of each subset, averaged with larger subsets counting more
symbols.infty: infinity: a bandwidth that grows without limit
symbols.sim: is drawn from (random noise follows this distribution)
symbols.w:normal: an attribute value for Humidity: normal
symbols.w:high: an attribute value for Humidity: high
symbols.w:weak: an attribute value for Wind: weak
symbols.w:sunny: an attribute value for Outlook: sunny
symbols.w:overcast: an attribute value for Outlook: overcast
symbols.w:rain: an attribute value for Outlook: rain
symbols.w:humidity: an attribute: how humid the day is
symbols.w:temperature: an attribute: the day's temperature, a number
symbols.w:no: the class label: tennis is not played

Decision tree representation.X: an input feature (such as length), or a true/false variable in a Boolean function
Decision tree representation.Y: a second true/false variable in a Boolean function
Decision tree representation.n: the number of true/false input variables (as in parity)
Decision tree representation.f: false: the branch where the test fails
Decision tree representation.t: true: the branch where the test passes

Entropy.X: a quantity that can take k possible values, each with some probability
Entropy.p: the probability (share) of one outcome or class
Entropy.S: a set of training examples whose class mix is measured
Entropy.H: entropy: the average bits needed to name the class, 0 if pure

Top-down induction.k: the number of clusters in k-means, another greedy method

Errors and disagreements.h: one class the example might belong to, summed over all classes

Gini impurity.p: the share of examples in the node that belong to class j

Information gain.X: an input feature; X_A is the value an example has for attribute A
Information gain.S: the set of examples being split; S_nu is the part with value nu

Gain ratio.m: the number of branches (equal-sized) an attribute splits into
Gain ratio.S: the set of examples being split; S_nu is the part with value nu

Costs.x: the example (its attribute values) we are predicting for
Costs.h: one class the example might truly have, summed over all classes
Costs.H: the set of all classes the example might belong to
Costs.R: expected loss: average cost of taking action alpha given x
Costs.A: an attribute whose measurement has a cost
Costs.i: numbers the possible actions (predictions) we could take

Continuous attributes.n: the number of distinct values of the numeric attribute
Continuous attributes.t: true: the test (such as temperature above a threshold) passes

Missing values.n: the node whose test uses the attribute with the missing value
Missing values.p: the probability assigned to one value of the attribute
Missing values.i: counts the possible values of the attribute
Missing values.v: one possible value of the attribute

Regression trees.Y: the set of target values of the examples at a node
Regression trees.y: the target value of one example in the subset
Regression trees.i: counts the subsets (groups) a threshold creates
Regression trees.j: counts the examples inside one subset
Regression trees.m: the number of examples in subset Y_i
Regression trees.w: the share of examples in subset i (its size divided by the total)
Regression trees.R: a rectangular region of the inputs; the tree predicts one level there
Regression trees.c: the single constant a leaf predicts to minimise squared error

Model trees.x: the input feature, used both for splitting and as the regression variable
Model trees.y: the output (target) value, such as the curve cos(pi x) being approximated
Model trees.T: the set of target values at a node; T_i are the subsets after a split
Model trees.i: counts the subsets after the split

Linear smoothing.x: the input value; x_0 is the query point we predict at
Linear smoothing.X: the input value of one training point
Linear smoothing.Y: the target value of one training point
Linear smoothing.i: counts training points (in the weighted sum)
Linear smoothing.j: counts training points (in the denominator that normalises the weights)
Linear smoothing.k: the number of nearest neighbours that get weight 1/k in kNN
Linear smoothing.w: the weight training point i gets for a query x: weights add to 1
Linear smoothing.y: the target value being predicted or smoothed
Linear smoothing.hat:y: the kNN regression prediction: a weighted average of training targets
Linear smoothing.abs: absolute value: the distance of u from zero
Linear smoothing.f: the true function, here sin(4x), that the smoother estimates

Formula sheet.x: the query point or example we predict for
Formula sheet.i: counts subsets or branches (or training points in the smoother)
Formula sheet.j: counts classes (or training points in the smoother denominator)
Formula sheet.m: the number of examples in a subset
Formula sheet.n: the number of values of a numeric attribute (or training points)
Formula sheet.T: the set of target values at a node; T_i the subsets after the split
Formula sheet.Y: the target values of a group of examples; Y_i is one training target in the smoother
Formula sheet.S: the set of examples at the node; S_nu the part with value nu

Code you should recognise.m: the number of examples in the data

Worked examples.A: a true/false variable (or a column of 0 and 1 values)
Worked examples.E: the entropy of a child set, as a number
Worked examples.N: number of No examples, as in [0Y,2N]
Worked examples.Y: number of Yes examples, as in [3Y,2N]
Worked examples.x: the input value (such as temperature, or the cosine input)
Worked examples.y: the output value, such as price or the line being fitted
Worked examples.f: false in a tree test; elsewhere the true function sin(4x)
Worked examples.S: the set of examples being split
Worked examples.H: entropy of a set with the given share of Yes

Exam traps.h: the bandwidth of the kernel smoother
